$comment: How a frame shows a fish's photo so it keeps the fish (packages/schema/src/image-geometry.ts subjectFrame; the Design Lead's look for each frame: docs of the frames board). For a frame of `ratio` (width over height) and a photo `w` by `h` with the fish's `box` (fractions of the photo from its top-left corner, as `box` and `imgBox` carry it): the frame covers the photo with a window of its shape, which cuts one side of the photo only. The fish's loss is the share of the box's length along that side that falls outside the window. (1) The centred window, if it loses `cut` or less (plus `slack`, so the last bit of a window's edge can't turn exactly `cut` into more); (2) else the window centred on the box, kept inside the photo, if it loses `cut` or less; (3) else the photo whole. No box (null): the centred window, never whole. `frame`: {"fit": "cover", "x", "y"} places the window as CSS object-position does (its offset over the room it has to move, 0.5 where it has none), or {"fit": "whole"}. Every box's edges fall on whole pixels at its photo's size, so a reader computing in fractions and the site in pixels decide on the same box; positions agree to `tolerance`. Generated by packages/schema/test/photo-crop-vectors.test.ts from the site's rule: edit a case's inputs here (note, w, h, box, ratio), then run UPDATE_VECTORS=1 on that test file, which writes every frame and `cut`; the test fails while the file differs from what the rule gives. The app's tests hold its own rule and its own cut to this file.

cases.note: no box (none found yet, or no animal): today's centred crop
a small fish in the middle: centred
exactly 5%, centred (a 2:1 frame over a square photo): stays centred
5.1%, centred: the window moves onto the fish and loses none
exactly 5% once moved, the window's edge between pixels (19:25): it still covers
a box on the photo's left edge: the window goes to that edge
a box in a corner, on two edges: the window goes to the right edge
a fish longer than any crop of a square frame: whole
the same fish in a 16:9 frame: centred
a frame wider than the photo: the window cuts top and bottom, and moves up to the fish
a tall photo in a 4:3 tile, the fish near the top: the window goes to the top
a box of the whole photo, in another shape: whole
a box of the whole photo, in a frame of its own shape: centred
kribensis's head (the owner's report) in a 4:3 tile: whole
Cyprichromis leptosoma's head (the owner's report) in a 4:3 tile: whole
Fuelleborn's head in a 4:3 tile: the moved crop mends it
Fuelleborn's head on a fish page's square top (the Design Lead's board): whole
Maingano's head on a fish page's square top (the Design Lead's board): whole
